newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude oil steady but spreads slip slowly low.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude oil steady but spreads slip slowly low.

text.p: North Sea crude markets were steady though quiet on Wednesday but inter-month spreads and nearby CFDs eased later.
The one Brent cargo which turned wet (loading May 8-10) was kept by the Shell group.
May 2-4 and May 6-8 Brent cargoes were sold by a refiner to a large trader at an undisclosed June related price.
A cargo of May 18-20 Statfjord was talked to have been sold by the equity holder at a strong dated Brent +15 cents though there was no confirmation.
A large trader was heard to be sending a VLCC of mainly pre-sold early May Brent to the Mediterranean.
The U.S. Gulf still remained a viable market for Brent with offers around June WTI -80 cents.
Kirkuk was seen by Mediterranean refiners as an attractive option relative to pricey Urals.
"It's attractive and a good grade to buy and looks like it is going to trade at a good price this month," one Med refiner said.
